issues.description: The stretch question about f(x) = x·D(x) being continuous at exactly one point is beyond AP scope and may confuse advanced AP students. While intellectually interesting, it references the Dirichlet function which is not part of the AP curriculum.
issues.suggested_fix: Consider labeling it more explicitly as 'beyond AP' or replacing with a stretch question more aligned to AP-level content (e.g., constructing a function continuous at one endpoint but not the other).

issues.description: The description of discontinuity types says 'The type of discontinuity is named after which condition broke,' but this is slightly misleading. A removable discontinuity can also occur when condition 1 fails (hole with no value defined), not only when condition 3 fails. The text only illustrates condition 3 failing for removable discontinuities.
issues.suggested_fix: Add a brief note that a removable discontinuity can also arise when condition 1 fails (i.e., f(a) is simply undefined but the limit exists), or adjust the framing to say 'which condition broke first' rather than implying a strict one-to-one mapping.

issues.description: The deep dive on pointwise vs uniform continuity and the Heine-Cantor theorem is well beyond AP Calculus AB/BC scope. While deep dives are allowed to go further, this one goes quite far without flagging that it's entirely outside the AP curriculum.
issues.suggested_fix: Add a brief note at the top such as 'This topic goes beyond the AP Calculus syllabus but provides insight into why continuity on closed intervals is so powerful in the theorems you use.'

issues.description: The concept lists prerequisites as an empty array [], yet the advanced explanation references Taylor expansions, epsilon-delta definitions, and the derivative definition. While these are forward references rather than prerequisites, having zero prerequisites listed may confuse the app's dependency system since limits are clearly a prerequisite.
issues.suggested_fix: Add appropriate prerequisite concept IDs for limits (e.g., limits.definition or similar) to the prerequisites array.

issues.description: Contains a checkmark character (✓) which, while not an emoji, is close to the spirit of the 'no emojis' style rule and may render inconsistently.
issues.suggested_fix: Replace ✓ with a text equivalent like 'confirmed' or 'checks out' or simply remove it.

summary: Mathematically sound and pedagogically strong across all tiers; only minor issues with scope flagging, a slight oversimplification in discontinuity type classification, empty prerequisites array, and a stray checkmark character.
